notes: API1:2023 n/a: no auth or tenancy, the reference is the only key.
API2:2023 n/a: authentication is out of scope.
API5:2023 n/a: no roles. POST /policies/{ref}/renewals would be a privileged or agent-only function in a real deployment.
API10:2023 n/a: no upstream APIs. Grep for HttpClient and WebRequest in src/ found nothing.

API3:2023 met: RenewPolicyRequest is a separate DTO with only amount and paymentMethod. Strict JSON (UnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow) means startDate, version, end date or payment reference are rejected with 400. The enum converter has allowIntegerValues:false, so an undefined PaymentMethod value cannot reach the Mapperly switch. The response is the existing PolicyResponse, which has no Version or internal ids. The Version token is Persistence-only: the mapper ignores it and it is not in Contracts/.

API4:2023 met: the renewals route has [EnableRateLimiting("writes")]. The body is a small DTO under the server-wide 64 KB limit. The amount is shape-capped at 1,000,000.00 and 2 decimal places, matching the HasPrecision(18,2) columns. It adds no string fields, no collection and no list endpoint. An empty body gives 400, not 415 or 500.

API6:2023 met, double renewal: Policy.Renew measures the window from LatestTerm.End. After a renewal the latest term ends a year later, so a second renewal fails RENEW-1/2 until that term's own window. A cancelled policy returns RENEW-6 (409) alone.

API6:2023 met, concurrency: PolicyConfiguration marks Version as a concurrency token. UpdateTrackedRecords bumps Version whenever a term is appended (the changed set). A stale write throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException, which becomes PersistenceConflictException and then 409 /problems/concurrency. This covers concurrent renew vs renew and renew vs cancel.

API6:2023 met, payment integrity: the renewal Payment is built with the term's own amount (new Payment(ref, method, amount) and new Term(start, amount, payment)). It is a single decimal value, so payment.Amount equals term.Amount by construction. An unpaid term (no auto-renew) gets a null payment, and RENEW-3b rejects a client-supplied method. Cheque on auto-renew is rejected (COULD-3). The payment reference comes from the server-side generator.

API6:2023 met, renew-then-cancel: RefundCalculator.ForTerm refunds at most term.Amount per term (full amount for a future term, prorated for the current one, 0 for an unpaid term or a claim). Because each payment amount equals its term amount, the total refund is at most the sum of payments. Cancel is blocked after the first cancellation (CANCEL-4, 409), and Cancel7 checks against LatestTerm.End. The quote path does not call SaveChanges.

API8:2023 met: no new logging, no exception messages in ProblemDetails, and no developer exception page. UnexpectedExceptionHandler maps BadHttpRequestException and the concurrency conflict to fixed text. No secrets or connection strings in the diff.

API9:2023 met: the real E6 controller action replaces the stub. gate.stubs shows no NotImplementedException in src/, and gate.run shows Postman F4 Renew 54 requests with 0 failed. I did not inspect the OpenAPI document itself (light check).

NET: no raw SQL (grep for FromSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlRaw and SqlQueryRaw found nothing). Money is decimal throughout and no double or float appears. There are no DateTime.Now, UtcNow or Today calls; the service uses UkCalendar.Today(clock). gate.vulnerable reports 8 projects and none vulnerable. There are no package changes in the diff. The only logging call sites log method, path and status, with no personal data or bodies.

Observation, not a finding: Policy.Renew reads CurrentTerm(today).Payment!.Method when AutoRenew is true. That is safe today because every term of an auto-renewing policy is created with a payment. It would throw a NullReferenceException if stored data ever broke that invariant.
